claims.text: Enteral nutrition needs a functioning GI tract.
claims.quote: Enteral nutrition is indicated for patients who have a functioning gastrointestinal (GI) tract but cannot ingest enough nutrients orally

claims.text: Tube feeding for more than 4–6 weeks: place a gastrostomy or jejunostomy tube.
claims.quote: If tube feeding is expected to last > 4 to 6 weeks, consider a gastrostomy or jejunostomy tube, placed endoscopically, surgically, or radiologically.

claims.text: A jejunostomy tube does not lower aspiration risk compared with a gastrostomy tube.
claims.quote: Risk of tracheobronchial aspiration with jejunostomy tubes is as high as with gastrostomy tubes.

claims.text: Parenteral nutrition when the GI tract doesn't work or needs complete bowel rest.
claims.quote: PN may be the only feasible option for patients who do not have a functioning GI tract or who have disorders requiring complete bowel rest
Short bowel syndrome due to surgery

claims.text: Central PN needs a central venous access device (osmolarity >900 mOsm/L).
claims.quote: Central PN requires a central venous access device for safe infusion because solutions formulated for central PN have an osmolarity > 900 mOsm/L.

claims.text: Peripheral PN osmolarity should be ≤900 mOsm/L.
claims.quote: The osmolarity of the solution should be ≤ 900 mOsm/L.

claims.text: Hepatic: liver dysfunction, painful hepatomegaly, hyperammonemia.
claims.quote: Hepatic complications include liver dysfunction, painful hepatomegaly, and hyperammonemia.
